name: How do construction changes affect the final fourplex budget?

mainEntity.name: How much can change orders increase the cost of a fourplex project?
mainEntity.text: How much can change orders increase the cost of a fourplex project?

acceptedAnswer.text: This is a high-value unanswered question because many owners only hear the base bid and do not understand how much the final number can drift. Change orders can come from owner upgrades, field conditions, permit comments, or coordination gaps between consultants and contractors. A good answer should explain how to track changes, approve them carefully, and separate scope growth from genuine correction work. Searchers also need to know that a low initial bid can be misleading if it excludes many items that later appear as extras. A practical page should show how better preconstruction coordination reduces cost volatility. That makes the answer useful for both budgeting and hiring decisions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Change orders can raise fourplex costs quickly if they involve structural revisions, utility changes, finish upgrades, or permit rework. The more complete the drawings and scope are at the start, the lower the change-order risk tends to be.
